column3: Thousands of life-size clay soldiers, horses and chariots stand guard at the tomb of Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor. Each soldier has a different face. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A Ming-dynasty wall, about 14 kilometers around, that is among the best preserved in China. You can walk or cycle along the top, on a wide road.
A Tang-dynasty pagoda built in 652 to store the Buddhist scriptures that the monk Xuanzang brought back from India.
A slimmer Tang pagoda in the city, famous for its fine shape, and known for a deep crack that once closed after an earthquake.
A Ming-dynasty tower at the center of the old city, where a big bell was rung to mark the morning.
A tower that stands near the Bell Tower, where a huge drum was beaten at dusk to tell the time.
A busy lane of snack stalls and shops in the old Muslim neighborhood, with mutton skewers, sweets and the smell of spices.
A hot spring palace at the foot of Mount Li, tied to Emperor Xuanzong and his favorite, Yang Guifei, as described in a famous poem.
A grand museum with treasures such as Tang gold and silver, murals and ancient bronzes, which shows the story of Shaanxi and China.
A forest of stone steles with calligraphy by the greatest masters, and the Confucian classics, carved in stone over a thousand years.
One of the Five Sacred Mountains, with sheer granite cliffs. A path of planks hangs over the abyss, one of the most thrilling hikes in China.
Braised, chopped meat tucked in a crisp, chewy flatbread, often called a Chinese hamburger, a staple of Xi'an street food.
Cool, slippery noodles made from wheat or rice starch, tossed with chili oil, vinegar, cucumber and sesame paste.
A bowl of lamb soup in which you tear a flatbread into small pieces, and which is then cooked into a rich meal. A Xi'an classic.
Wide, hand-pulled noodles topped with chili flakes, garlic and scallions, then splashed with sizzling hot oil.
A sweet fried cake made from persimmons, a Xi'an treat with a soft center and crisp shell.
Noodles in a sour and spicy sauce with diced meat and vegetables, a Shaanxi classic, often served at weddings and festivals.
Qin opera is a loud, powerful local opera, one of the oldest in China, sung with strong, high voices.
A theater of leather puppets with a lamp behind a screen, and a skilled team of artists make them move and sing.
An old style of ensemble music with drums and wind instruments, which has links to the Tang court.
A Han-dynasty tomb complex with thousands of small clay figures buried in pits, and a museum below the ground.
The shared tomb of Emperor Gaozong and Empress Wu Zetian, with a Sacred Way lined with giant stone figures.
Thin noodles cooked on a pan and served with a savory, fragrant sauce, a Xianyang specialty.
A temple that houses a finger-bone relic of the Buddha, found in an underground vault with Tang treasures.
The highest peak in the Qinling Mountains, with a range of climates from forest to snowy rocks and a sea of cloud.
The classic Qishan version of saozi noodles, with a thin, springy noodle in a hot, sour, savory soup.
Cool noodles made from rolled dough, tossed in chili oil, vinegar and sauce, a street snack from Baoji.
The Yellow River squeezes into a narrow gorge and falls into it with a roar, like water pouring from a teapot.
Shredded potato tossed with flour, steamed and then mixed with chili and garlic, a simple dish from northern Shaanxi.
A sweet steamed cake of yellow millet, a staple of the Loess Plateau.
The tomb of Zhuge Liang, the brilliant strategist of the Three Kingdoms, who is a symbol of loyalty and wisdom.
Steamed rice noodles served warm with a spicy sauce, a Hanzhong breakfast.
A soft tofu made with the leaves of local vegetables, a Hanzhong specialty with a unique flavor.
The largest desert lake in China, a wide lake with water birds beside the Mu Us sandy land.
A Ming and Qing walled city on the edge of the desert, once a frontier garrison, with watchtowers and old streets.
Noodles in a hot lamb broth, a staple of northern Shaanxi's cold winters.
Tofu made with local water, firm and fine, a specialty that is cooked in a variety of ways.
A flaky pastry with a sweet filling, made in Pucheng for generations.
Crisp and sweet winter jujubes that ripen late in the year in Dali, a juicy fruit that is popular as a snack.
Walnuts grown on the mountain slopes of Shangluo, rich and oily and used in snacks and cooking.
Noodles steamed on a rack and then dressed with a spicy sauce, a favorite in Ankang.
A tea from Ziyang, grown in selenium-rich soil, a green tea with a clear, mellow taste.
